item.title: Wakayama Ramen: The Pork-and-Soy Bowl of Kishu — Guide
item.description: Wakayama ramen, known to locals simply as chuka soba, is one of Japan’s classic regional bowls: a broth blending pork bones and soy sauce into something rich, dark brown and deeply savoury, served with thin straight noodles, chashu pork, menma and spring onion. Its most charming tradition is the counter service: bowls of hayazushi (pressed mackerel sushi) and boiled eggs sit ready on the table, and diners help themselves while waiting, paying by the honour system at the end.
